newsitem.title: UK: UK won't let spending rise dramatically - Heseltine. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: UK won't let spending rise dramatically - Heseltine. [CORRECTED 20:20 GMT]

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative party will not try to buy the next general election with unearned tax cuts, or by letting public spending rise dramatically, Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said on Friday.
(Corrects to clarify government will not make any major increases in spending)
He told a rally in Leeds, northern England, that the government was determined to keep reducing its budget deficit with the aim of eliminating it in the medium term.
"We will not throw away the brightest prospects for a generation by letting public spending rip," he said.
Next week, the cabinet meets to decide the level of public spending in the budget, which is set for November 26.
Repeating the standard position of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke, Heseltine said the budget would not include any tax cuts that could not be afforded.
"We're not in the business of trying to buy the next election with tax cuts that haven't been earned and can't be sustained. We will only cut taxes when it is prudent to do so," Heseltine said.
He said the government, which must call an election by May 22, was delivering a "Rolls Royce" recovery that was built to last.

"I am personally convinced that at the next general election the British public will vote to protect the economic gains of the last 17 years so that we can look forward to five more prosperous years under a fifth consecutive Conservative government," Heseltine said.
